ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the isosceles triangle $ABC$, where $AB=AC$, $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, intersecting $AB$ at point $E$ and $AC$ at point $D$. If $\angle ADE=40^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CBD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $DE$ bisects $AB$ perpendicularly,\\
hence $AD=BD$, $\angle AED=90^\circ$,\\
given $\angle ADE=40^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABD=\angle A=50^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle ABC=\angle C=\frac{1}{2}\times(180^\circ-50^\circ)=65^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle CBD=65^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{15^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; D is located on side AC, and E is located on side AB. Segment DE connects from D to E, and there is a right-angle mark at E, indicating that DE is perpendicular to AB; segment BD is also drawn. Reasoning: It is known that DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, and D is on DE, so the distances from D to the two points A and B are equal, namely AD = BD. Also because DE is perpendicular to AB, ∠AED = 90°. In right triangle ADE, it is known that ∠ADE = 40°, therefore ∠DAE = 180° - 90° - 40° = 50°. Since D is on AC and E is on AB, ∠DAE is the vertex angle ∠BAC of triangle ABC, so ∠BAC = 50°. Also ABC is an isosceles triangle, AB = AC, therefore the base angles ∠ABC = ∠BCA = (180° - 50°) / 2 = 65°. In triangle ABD, AD = BD, so it is also an isosceles triangle, ∠ABD = ∠DAB = 50°. Therefore ∠CBD = ∠ABC - ∠ABD = 65° - 50° = 15°.
